minutes.headline: Commissioners voted to hire a surveyor to mark the 400-foot well radius at Hickory Hills; a used loader was also discussed.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners reviewed warrants, discussed a used loader bought for the district, and shared impressions of a site visit to the Townsend PFAS treatment plant. They voted on a surveyor quote to mark the 400-foot radius around the Hickory Hills well, and agreed to push ahead with the InvoiceCloud payment changes despite a delay. A resident questioned the loader purchase and the engineering approach, and radio equipment delays were discussed.

what_happened.line: Commissioners voted to hire a surveyor to mark the well radius at the Hickory Hills well, and the motion passed.
Commissioners said they want permanent pins, rebar or steel, rather than stakes, to mark the well radius.
Commissioners agreed to proceed with the InvoiceCloud payment change even though it takes effect at the end of January rather than January 1.
Commissioners were open to the superintendent getting prices from other vendors for installing radio equipment; no resolution was reached.
A used loader bought for the district was reported, paid from the water maintenance and equipment account, and a resident questioned the purchase in public comment.

why_it_matters: Marking the protective radius around the Hickory Hills well is a step toward the district formally claiming control of the land around the well, which bears on keeping that water source protected.
The InvoiceCloud change alters how water bills can be paid, and its delay to the end of January means customers get the new payment options later than first planned.
The loader purchase and the radio installation are district spending that residents may see raised again, since the loader drew a public question and installation may have to go out to bid.
watch_next: The surveyor's marking of the well radius at Hickory Hills, and whether the district then moves to claim the area around the well.
